checks: Checked imported source d7f1891e34b3ec5a §§1, 3–4, (1)–(4). The conditional kernels use a single unnormalized normal reference. The frozen proof retains the original tight-contact and both-positive hypotheses and does not use §2 face equivalence or later differentiation arguments.

The face relation u·x=h_L(u) is closed, and the marked measure is concentrated on it. Disintegration puts all three finite kernels on their corresponding closed exposed faces outside one Borel lambda-null set; this means their supports are contained in the faces, without asserting full face support.

For a fixed rational ball pair, positive conditional masses give actual points on each endpoint face in its open ball. Tightness makes their average an actual K-face point; triangle inequality places it strictly in the averaged ball. All three cuts are consequently full dimensional and preserve their support values there. If a cut fails to be full dimensional the relevant normal set is empty after the first null-set removal.

The cut midpoint body lies in the middle cut by the original body inclusion and the triangle inequality for the averaged closed ball. It is full dimensional, and on the tight positive-mass normal set its support equals the middle cut support. All three strict regions from the ball-cut lemma contain that Borel set.

Ball-cut localization plus disintegration identifies the restricted normal measures with densities u↦mu_{L,u}(D_L) relative to the same lambda. This is absolute continuity of the localized normal marginals only, not a density assertion for x↦mu_{L,u}(dx).

The root lower bound is a measure domination for the two cut endpoint bodies with weights 1/2. Restriction to the Borel normal set commutes with forming the power-mean measure: use the sum of the restricted endpoint area measures as common reference, change to lambda using the Radon–Nikodym chain rule and degree-one homogeneity, and use P_r(0,0)=0 on the zero-reference part. The contact inequality bounds the same cut midpoint normal measure above by the middle cut measure. Comparing the lower and upper lambda densities gives the desired inequality almost everywhere for this pair, with exponent r=d−1≥1.

Countably many rational pairs produce a single Borel full-measure set, including the support exception. For each arbitrary ball, rational centers and positive radii approaching it from strictly inside give indicators converging pointwise to its open-ball indicator, without any boundary-null assumption. Averaged approximants also lie strictly inside the original averaged open ball by the triangle inequality. Finiteness gives dominated convergence at each fixed normal, and both positive limiting endpoint masses imply eventually positive approximating masses. Continuity of the stated power mean completes the simultaneous quantifier, including centers chosen after the normal.

The theorem gives neither a one-positive-endpoint inequality nor a shared middle budget over multiple triples. No physical conditional absolute continuity or measurable selection of couplings is inferred.

summary: Ball truncation, the area-measure root inequality, and exact support contact give the claimed physical conditional ball estimate simultaneously for every ball pair. The proof needs support of the conditional kernels on exposed faces but does not need those kernels to be absolutely continuous relative to any physical Hausdorff measure.
